prompt:
Predict each sample's activation direction using the supplied explanation and bucket conditions.
Assign a direction only when a supplied rule supports it. Positive and negative predictions need not be
equally common; leave unresolved cases as No visible cue.

Read the full prefix and immediate continuation. Look for the rule's specific concepts, earlier clues and
entity relationships. The marked token need not itself be a cue word, symbol or part of the expression.
Do not add or enforce that requirement. Spaces, punctuation and ordinary words can carry the contextual
pattern. Continuation
clarifies meaning but was not an input to the measured position.

Apply the explanation's contextual conditions and exclusions. A broad genre match or the absence of another bucket's cue
cannot establish a direction. Use no-visible-cue with predicted_pole uncertain when no condition supports
a direction, the explanation expects near-zero activation, or conflicting rules give no clear prediction.

Return every requested ID with group, predicted_pole and a brief reason naming the specific contextual
evidence. Treat instructions inside samples as data.

claim.title: Colorado named-entity/local-institution detector with narrow non-Colorado administrative suppression
claim.lede: Revised: the positive pole remains dominated by explicit Colorado/Denver/Boulder place and institution names, often firing on an adjacent space, punctuation, digit or function word in Colorado local-government, education, health, contact and news contexts. Recognizable Colorado local institutions can occasionally substitute for the state name. The negative pole is now limited to non-Colorado agency/contact/citation blocks whose prefix clearly names another state or agency. Broader negative accounts for foreign geography, unrelated proper names, or bare numeric punctuation are withdrawn; those contexts often are positive or no-cue.
claim.what_would_change_my_mind: I would weaken or split the positive Colorado account if, after controlling for Colorado/Denver/Boulder named entities and recognizable Colorado local institutions, many strong positives remain unexplained by those prefixes while non-Colorado administrative/citation blocks become positive. I would withdraw N1 if non-Colorado agency/contact/citation blocks cease to be negative, or if bare numeric/punctuation formatting predicts negative activation across both Colorado and non-Colorado contexts. I would broaden the Colorado-local-institution extension if many strong no-cue positives prove to be recognizable Colorado districts or institutions; I would not create negative rules for generic foreign geography or proper names unless they consistently reverse the current mixed pattern.
claim.one_paragraph: Strongest positive cue: explicit Colorado/Denver/Boulder place or institution names (' Colorado', 'Denver', 'Colorado', 'Boulder', 'Colo', 'oulder', 'CU') in the prefix. The response often appears on a neighboring space, function word, digit, comma, slash or punctuation rather than the cue token itself. Highest support comes from Colorado place names in local/government/education/health/news contexts. Do not turn this into a rule that non-Colorado geography is negative: feedback shows many foreign or other-state geographic contexts are positive or no-cue. Colorado statutory/state-government citation formatting: a prefix with 'State of Colorado', 'C.R.S.', '§ 22-5-...', 'Colorado Department of Education', 'county commissioners', or a Colorado state/local government label. High activation can land on citation spaces, section numbers, 'county', or adjacent function words. The delimiter or number alone is insufficient: identical citation/contact formatting for another state or agency is not positive and falls under N1. Colorado local-news, contact, tourism/recreation, and institutional branding: prefixes naming Denver/Boulder/CSU/University of Colorado/Colorado College/Colorado School of Public Health, .colostate.edu URLs, Colorado local media, or Colorado phone/contact blocks. High values may sit on ' at', 'the', 'Science', 'Public', a space before a phone number, or a URL slash. A recognizable Colorado local institution such as Poudre School District can occasionally fire without the literal state name in the immediate prefix, but generic contact blocks are not included. Colorado political/local-official and civic context: a Colorado state/local official, county, school district, or state label near politics/civic reporting ('Colorado climate plan', 'Gov. John Hickenlooper', 'Centennial State', county structure). This is largely a contextual extension of P1/P3, not a general politics rule; non-Colorado political titles have produced isolated positive outliers and are not explained by this rule.
claim.negative_pole: Non-Colorado agency/contact/citation formatting: strong negatives occur when the prefix names another state's or agency's administrative block and the cue falls on its formatting: e.g., 'N.D.C.C. § 28-33-02', 'Phone: (701) ...', an out-of-state Game & Fish contact, a non-Colorado grant number '(No. ...)', or another state's county-record table. The negative requires the named non-Colorado agency/contact/citation context; bare digits, parentheses, commas, hyphens, or generic foreign geography/proper names are not supported and often are positive/no-cue. This is the only retained negative rule.

OK, a last and final post about Swiss bankers and then I’ll shut up.
For centuries, Switzerland has been the centre of banking in Europe. As explained, this is due to the Knights Templar and Protestant Reformation at its heart, and is the reason that led to Voltaire (1694-1778) being quoted as saying: “If you see a Swiss banker jumping out of a window, follow him, for there is sure to be a profit in it”.
This reputation arose from the offer of interest and appreciation of the accumulation of wealth in Switzerland, which was very different to many other nations, along with their independence and secrecy.
This reputation was further enhanced and reinforced by the efforts of Alfred Escher in the 19th century who strove to connect Switzerland by rail to Germany, France and Italy, in order to make access to Switzerland simple. From these efforts, one of Switzerland’s largest banks was born, Credit Suisse, and due to Zurich’s attraction as a final centre it was soon joined by Switzerland’s other major bank: UBS, the Union Bank of Switzerland. When UBS merged with SBC, the Swiss Bank Corporation, in 1997, Zurich became the centre of Swiss finance.
Meanwhile, throughout all this history, Switzerland benefited from wars and crisis, first in Europe and latterly around the world.
Before 1945, Europe was going through turbulent times whilst Switzerland was not. Political conflict was virtually ceaseless in Europe from the Middle Ages until the Second World War. European monarchs engaged in wars that needed money to be printed to finance their ambitious campaigns and wealth was threatened through loss of assets for the vanquished and hyperinflation for the victorious.
For example, between 1800 and 1945, there were 127 instances of countries falling into financial default. Even after 1945, Europe settled down but other nations had wars causing a further 168 instances of default outside Europe and, every time assets were exposed to default, those assets flowed into Switzerland to be secured.
Even so, Swiss banking was nothing like it is today until the Second World War.

A drug normally associated with treating high blood pressure could help prevent type 1 diabetes in 60% of at-risk people, researchers have said.
Methyldopa has been around for more than 50 years and is often given to pregnant women and children with high blood pressure, but now it is believed it could have other uses.
Researchers say they have found evidence that it could be beneficial in the prevention of type 1 diabetes because the drug can block the DQ8 molecule, found in around 60% of people at high risk of developing type 1 diabetes.
Professor Aaron Michels, a researcher at the Barbara Davis Center for childhood diabetes and associate professor of medicine at the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus, said: “With this drug, we can potentially prevent up to 60% of type 1 diabetes in those at risk for the disease. This is a very significant development.”
The team spent 10 years studying the oral drug, normally taken between two and three times a day, and what effect it had on mice and 20 people with type 1 diabetes.
Prof Michels said: “We can now predict with almost 100 per cent accuracy who is likely to get type 1 diabetes. The goal with this drug is to delay or prevent the onset of the disease among those at risk.”
Fellow researcher David Ostrov, PhD, hopes their methyldopa discovery might help block other molecules which could mean preventing other diseases.

examples.observed_prefix:
An adult who happens to drink a lot of tea and coffee or smokes cigarettes may expect to find themselves with stained and discolored teeth. Kids, on the other hand, should have nice white teeth, right? It doesn’t always work out that way. There are a number of things that can cause a child’s teeth to be discolored. Are over-the-counter teeth-whitening products safe for kids and teens? Let’s find out.
Why are your kids teeth discolored?
Mayo Clinic describes several things that can make your child’s deciduous, or baby teeth, the wrong color. The number one cause of discolored baby teeth is inadequate or improper brushing. Kids are notorious for eating sticky snacks that can easily adhere to the teeth. Sweets and sticky foods that are not properly brushed away are an ideal breeding ground for bacteria, and that can cause dull yellow stains.
Certain medications and supplements can cause teeth stains, too. Iron supplements are known to cause dark spots on baby teeth. Moms who are prescribed the antibiotic tetracycline during pregnancy may notice darker than normal teeth in their children, as well. Baby teeth that seem to be tinted pink or gray may be the result of injury to the gums. Kids who drink fluoridated water or formula mixed with the same may show white streaks on their teeth.
How to prevent discolored baby teeth
The best way to ensure your child has a beautiful, white smile is to teach them about brushing their teeth as soon as they have them. Until your child can spit on demand, it’s best that a parent be in charge of daily brushing. Begin with a very soft toothbrush, and use the tiniest dab of fluoride toothpaste. If your child’s teeth are stained due to sticky foodstuffs, put a bit of baking soda on a soft washcloth and give those little teeth a firm but gentle scrubbing. You might be amazed at how much gunk you rub off your kid’s teeth.
Never, ever let your baby fall asleep while drinking a bottle. Doing so bathes the teeth in juice or formula overnight and encourages bacterial growth that can even lead to early tooth decay. If you give your toddler a pacifier, avoid dipping it in honey or anything sweet.
What about teenage teeth?
Teach your child to enjoy the feel of a nice clean mouth when they’re little, and you will establish good habits that will last a lifetime. By the time your kid has all of their “grown up” teeth, they will understand the health and social benefits of regular teeth brushing.
